item.title: NZDUSD buyers defend the floor. Can they break the ceiling?
item.description:
The NZDUSD moved lower after weaker New Zealand jobs data early in the new trading day, but sellers could not push the price below a familiar floor near 0.5579 (see green circles on the chart below). That level has attracted buyers on a number of occasions going back to late September and through October. Today, buyers leaned against it again and were rewarded with a rebound as the market reacted to the US election results.

The hold matters technically. Buyers had a level to define and limit risk, and they defended it. However, holding support is only the first step. To increase the bullish bias, they now need to take back resistance above.

The 200-hour moving average stalled the rebound

The rally today off the solid floor, broke above its 100 hour moving average near 0.5622, but ran into the falling 200-hour moving average (green line) near 0.56418. Sellers leaned against that level and stalled the move higher, keeping that moving average as a key topside barometer.

Get above—and stay above—and buyers would give themselves more control. Until then, sellers can point to the failed test as evidence that overhead resistance is still doing its job.

Ahead of that level, the 100-hour moving average near 0.5622 and the swing area from 0.56256 to 0.56333 provide nearer hurdles. Buyers need to establish support above those levels to put the 200-hour moving average back in their sights.

What comes next?

A sustained break above the 200-hour moving average would open the door toward the next swing area between 0.56681 and 0.56860. Above that, remember 0.57085. The triple top near that level helped give sellers the confidence to push lower in October. It remains an important target if buyers can build on today’s rebound.

On the downside, 0.5579 remains the key floor. Hold above it, and buyers retain a foundation for another recovery attempt. Break below it, and the support that has repeatedly attracted buying would give way, opening the door toward the low near 0.5564.

For now, buyers defended the floor, but sellers defended the 200-hour moving average. The next directional clue comes from which side gives way.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: The market is making a big bet on ending the Iran war
item.description:
If endless Middle East wars were on the ballot, it's safe to say how it would have gone. 

Republicans are openly blaming the war for the midterm rout and the market is taking that at face value. The indication is that Trump will be forced out of Iran, and possibly soon. That will mean a reopened Hormuz and oil will be flowing again.

The market is aggressively pricing it in with WTI down $7.69 to $88.39 today in one of the largest plunges of the war. The close was the lowest since August 31. Given the oil hit $105 late last week, that's a huge turn. It's a big drag for inflation too and you can see that in the Treasury market with yields down 3-6 basis points, though there are certainly puts and takes there with Democrats now looking like they're destined to hold the Senate for the next 4-6 years.

I fear that a deal to end the war may prove difficult. Trump has been trying to extract the US from it for months with little success and I wonder how eager Iran will be to deal after the vote. If a deal is made, I also wonder how fast the oil can move and how quickly inventories can be rebuilt. Refineries are already running full-tilt and inventories have been drawn down heavily. 

Looking out the oil and gasoline futures curves, today's drops have been consistent so there is some real optimism there, but so many times during this war, that optimism has proven misplaced. There are leaks today about positive developments and there seems to be a deal on the table. The easiest thing right now may be for Trump to take what's available. His own party is likely to back any deal to extricate themselves from this blame game.

There is talk of a pre-emptive Iranian strike at the moment but it's tough to believe they would let this moment to negotiate go to waste.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Gold is taking it clue from the USD and yields moving lower. Technicals are also giving the buyers a push.
item.description:
Gold is trading up more than $130, or 3.3%, at $4061.80. The price reached a high of $4070.53 after trading as low as $3919.93.

Lower Treasury yields and a weaker US dollar are helping fuel the gains. The US 10-year yield is down 6.6 basis points at 4.883%, near its lowest level since September 10.

Why do lower yields and a weaker USD support gold?

A weaker USD makes gold less expensive for overseas buyers. Gold is priced internationally in dollars. When the dollar falls against currencies like the euro or yen, buyers using those currencies can purchase the same ounce for less, assuming the dollar gold price is unchanged. That can encourage demand.

Lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding gold. Gold pays no interest. When Treasury yields fall, investors give up less interest income by owning gold instead of bonds, making the precious metal relatively more attractive.

Technical support provided the foundation

Recall that Monday’s low tested the rising 100-week moving average and a lower channel trendline near $3870. Buyers leaned against that support and pushed the price higher, establishing a base for today’s advance.

Today, buyers strengthened their control by pushing above the 100-hour moving average at $3960 and the 200-hour moving average at $3993.19. Those breaks shifted the shorter-term bias higher and helped accelerate the move toward $4070.53.

The support held. Resistance broke. Buyers gained more control.

The next upside test comes near $4088

The downward-sloping upper channel trendline near $4088 is the next upside barometer. Sellers may lean against that level, with risk defined on a break above. After today’s sharp rally, it also gives buyers a level to consider taking some profit.

However, a break above that trendline—and an ability to stay above—would give buyers another reason to push higher. The next targets would be the 38.2% retracement at $4186, followed by the falling 100-day moving average near $4205.

What would weaken the bullish bias?

If sellers defend the upper channel trendline, attention would turn back toward the natural support at $4000 and the 200-hour moving average near $3993.

That area is now a key downside barometer. Holding above would keep the shorter-term bias tilted in the buyers’ favor. Moving back below would weaken that bias and bring the 100-hour moving average near $3960 back into focus.

Trading lesson: Let the technicals confirm the story

Lower yields and a weaker dollar provide a supportive fundamental backdrop, but the technicals help traders define the trade.

The bounce from weekly support gave buyers a place to lean against. The breaks above the hourly moving averages confirmed improving momentum. Now, the upper channel trendline near $4088 provides the next test.

Buyers need to break and stay above that resistance to extend their control. If they cannot, traders have a defined level to measure a potential rotation back toward support.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.
